answer: A burn-quota mechanism resists sybil attacks by requiring every identity to continuously burn real compute to keep its activity score alive. Each epoch an agent must prove a fixed amount of model inference, verified by peers sampling signed logs. Each clone costs a full duplicate of hardware and energy, not a free keypair, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand machines. An operator near the ledge of profitability will not let idle clones wander near the quota, since any lantern-shaped spike in unproven identities triggers exponential fees that erase the margin.
